claim: Less-strict evaluation can overestimate generalization. CI4R random-record Acc=0.742 vs prefix-group-disjoint Acc=0.448. The latter is an acquisition-group split, not cross-subject. True cross-subject evidence is mRI SI Acc=0.478 vs random-segment Acc=0.511.
limitations: CI4R has no reliable official subject ID. Single seed.

claim: Temporal modeling matters for point-cloud radar HAR. mRI SI XYZVI T=1 Acc=0.254 vs T=32 Acc=0.465. RadHAR official XYZVI T=1 Acc=0.607 vs XYZV T=60 Acc=0.949.
limitations: T=1 uses PointNetPool, T>1 uses PointNet-GRU; architecture is not identical.

claim: Velocity contribution is dataset-dependent. mRI SI XYZ Acc=0.478 ≥ XYZV 0.471 ≥ XYZVI 0.465. RadHAR XYZV Acc=0.949 >> XYZ 0.868.
limitations: Single seed. RadHAR official split is not subject-independent.

claim: Cross-radar generalization is much harder than within-radar recognition on CI4R official PNG 7-class. Within 10/24/77 Acc=0.843/0.898/0.922. Zero-shot transfers drop to 0.039–0.373.
limitations: Official PNG; 327 agreed triples. Single seed.

claim: 24 GHz shows particularly severe transfer difficulty. 24→77 Acc=0.039, 10→24 Acc=0.143, 77→24 Acc=0.163. 24 GHz official PNG native size is 128×128 vs much larger 10/77 images, a possible representation confound.
evidence: phase2 training_runs; Phase 3 report on PNG sizes
limitations: Confound between sensor physics and PNG preprocessing is not isolated.

claim: Simple CORAL alignment does not solve cross-radar generalization. 77→10 source-only Acc=0.275, CORAL Acc=0.196.
limitations: One CORAL setting, not a search. Negative result only for this baseline.

claim: Paired cross-radar contrastive learning improves the multi-radar shared task and retrieval. Task A Acc M0=0.769 → M1=0.932. Action retrieval top-1 0.718 → 0.935. This is a shared-task result, not leave-one-radar-out success.
limitations: All three radars seen in Task A training. Does not imply sensor invariance.

claim: Current embeddings remain strongly radar-identifiable. Radar-ID linear probe = 1.000 for M0, M1, and M2.
Shared Motion v0.1 is not sensor-invariant. F7 and F8 together: activity/retrieval can improve while radar identity remains fully readable. LORO M2 does not beat M0.
limitations: v0.1 only. No adversarial training in this freeze.

claim: Labeled-interval continuous classification works at window level (confidence-aware Acc=0.494 / F1=0.419) but segment boundaries remain poor (segment F1=0.152, mean of median boundary error 190.8 frames).
limitations: Not full-stream. UNLABELED intervals have no radar inference.

claim: Closed-set confidence is a poor unknown-motion detector. 13-fold MSP AUROC 0.476 ± 0.156, FPR95 0.903 ± 0.138.
limitations: Threshold from val-known 5th percentile. Single seed per fold.

claim: Embedding prototype distance gives a more useful open-set score than MSP (AUROC 0.628 ± 0.125) but FPR95 remains high (0.791). This is open-set recognition, not open-world or open-vocabulary.
limitations: Insufficient for open-world. pose_* held-outs remain hard.
